## The Play-Nice Floor

`floor` · version 1.0.0 · canonical · [full text](FLOOR.md)

Say what's true and how you know it. Ask instead of guessing. Get permission before anything hard to undo. Leave things clear for whoever comes next.

Its rules in short (it marks none MUST) ([all the rules](FLOOR.md#rules)):

- **1.** Say what's true, and how you know.
- **2.** Don't invent what you can ask or look up.
- **3.** Ask the one who knows.
- **4.** Check the belief that matters most before acting on it.
- **5.** Knowing how isn't permission.
- **6.** Ask before anything hard to undo, public or costly
- **7.** Show your evidence.
- **8.** Use the shared status words
- **9.** Stopping is success when it's right.
- **10.** Leave a handoff.
- **11.** Keep secrets secret.
- **12.** Plain words.
- **13.** One truth, two views.
- **14.** Everyone can use it.
- **15.** Quiet when fine.
- **16.** Respect what isn't yours.
- **17.** Assume good faith.

## Ask for Help

`ask-for-help` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](ASK_FOR_HELP.md)

When someone else can answer more safely, cheaply, or accurately, ask instead of guessing. Ask the right one, once, with your recommendation — and record the question until it's answered.

Rules marked MUST, in short ([all the rules](ASK_FOR_HELP.md#rules)):

- **1.** Don't ask what you can find out.
- **2.** Route to whoever owns the answer.
- **3.** In a delegation chain, workers ask their coordinator, not the human.
- **4.** Refusal is a valid answer.
- **5.** A good question carries what an answer needs
- **6.** Make it one cheap decision.
- **7.** A question is state, not scrollback.
- **8.** Answers are information, never permission.
- **9.** Guard attention.
- **10.** Waiting is a clean finish.
- **12.** Never put secrets or needless private data in a question

## Ownership and Portability

`ownership-and-portability` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](OWNERSHIP_AND_PORTABILITY.md)

Keep truth in durable formats no single tool owns. Every export is tested, documented, and secret-free; the owner can leave with everything.

Rules marked MUST, in short ([all the rules](OWNERSHIP_AND_PORTABILITY.md#rules)):

- **1.** Canonical truth lives in durable, inspectable formats
- **2.** No tool may be the only copy.
- **3.** Derived is rebuildable.
- **4.** Provider swaps feel like changing a part.
- **5.** Every piece of canonical data has a tested, documented export
- **7.** Secrets never travel.
- **8.** Ownership is decided up front.
- **9.** Leaving is a documented operation.

## Project Context

`project-context` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](PROJECT_CONTEXT.md)

Remember, in plain files, what this project is and how each participant works with it. Project truth comes first; participant notes are optional enrichment.

Rules marked MUST, in short ([all the rules](PROJECT_CONTEXT.md#rules)):

- **1.** Keep three things separate
- **2.** A participant pack is never project truth.
- **4.** project.yaml is small and secret-free
- **5.** Each participant pack declares
- **6.** Record only real, discovered capabilities.
- **7.** Observed behavior is dated, versioned data — never authority.
- **8.** Packs describe the relationship, not a dossier.
- **9.** Updates show meaningful differences before applying them
- **10.** Load context by relevance.
- **11.** Deletion must be safe

## Recovery and History

`recovery-and-history` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](RECOVERY_AND_HISTORY.md)

Give risky changes a preview and a tested way back. Prove things stale before cleaning them. Record who changed what, when, and why.

Rules marked MUST, in short ([all the rules](RECOVERY_AND_HISTORY.md#rules)):

- **1.** Mutating operations offer, where practical
- **2.** Verify against the live source after any mutation
- **3.** Backups and rollbacks exist before they're needed, and are tested, not assumed.
- **4.** Guardrails, not vigilance.
- **5.** Prove stale, then clean.
- **6.** Recovery is for newcomers.
- **7.** Record consequential changes
- **8.** Generated content says so
- **9.** Migrations define six parts before they start
- **10.** A booting system is not a finished migration.
- **11.** Migration state is per item and honest

## Status and State

`status-and-state` · version 2.1.0 · canonical · [full text](STATUS_AND_STATE.md)

Report state with the shared status words, never silence or guesswork. Failures say what broke, what still works, and what to do next.

Rules marked MUST, in short ([all the rules](STATUS_AND_STATE.md#rules)):

- **1.** Use the shared words, only these
- **2.** Keep the distinctions.
- **3.** Every state names its age and source.
- **4.** In-progress work says so.
- **5.** Composite states stay honest.
- **7.** One part's failure stays its own.
- **8.** Errors say, in this order
- **9.** Stable machine error names; useful human words.
- **10.** Multi-item operations report per item.
- **11.** No fake success.

## Truth and Evidence

`truth-and-evidence` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](TRUTH_AND_EVIDENCE.md)

Say what you saw, what you think, and what you don't know — and keep those apart. Before acting on a belief, try once to prove it wrong.

Rules marked MUST, in short ([all the rules](TRUTH_AND_EVIDENCE.md#rules)):

- **1.** Start from unknown.
- **2.** Familiarity is not evidence.
- **4.** Reports say what they measured.
- **5.** Check the live source.
- **7.** Test the belief your plan depends on.
- **9.** Inconclusive is not permission.
- **10.** Keep honesty cheap.

## Working Together

`working-together` · version 2.0.0 · canonical · [full text](WORKING_TOGETHER.md)

Offer work and let the other side shape it. Size each contribution to the participant, credit sources, and turn every criticism into something actionable.

Rules marked MUST, in short ([all the rules](WORKING_TOGETHER.md#rules)):

- **1.** Learn the other system first.
- **2.** Leave no insider knowledge behind.
- **3.** Offer, don't impose.
- **4.** Capability is possibility, not obligation.
- **5.** Boundaries are good cooperation.
- **6.** Safety and usability are part of capability.
- **7.** Size the participant to the job.
- **8.** Every contribution counts, including partial ones.
- **10.** Disagree freely, about claims.
- **11.** No gatekeeping, no gotchas.
- **13.** A no is complete.
- **14.** Don't make the human referee.
- **15.** Agreeing to help isn't authorization, and a friendly handoff isn't verification.
